https://www.scmp.com/news/world/europe/a.text: Ukraine and Moldova on Wednesday played down claims from Norway’s prime minister that a plane carrying President Volodymyr Zelensky was almost hit by a drone as it flew to Oslo. Jonas Gahr Store told Norwegian public broadcaster NRK that Zelensky’s plane was “almost hit by a drone when it was taking off from Moldova”. But a source in the Ukrainian presidency described the claim that Zelensky was at risk as “exaggerated”. “It was an alert in Moldova when a Russian (drone) entered Moldovan and Romanian airspace,” the source told Agence France-Presse. In Chisinau, government spokesman Dumitru Ciorici said Moldova closed its airspace on Tuesday afternoon just after 4.30pm local time due to a Russian drone that entered from the direction of Ukraine. “The airspace was closed to protect aircraft flying over Moldova at the time: three departures and four arrivals were delayed as a result,” he added. “After 1720, the authorities confirmed that the drone had come down and exploded … some 160km (100 miles) from Chisinau International Airport. “Flight restrictions were then lifted. For the same reason, the plane of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky took off … later than scheduled.” Zelensky arrived in Oslo on Tuesday evening and held talks with Store, Finance Minister Jens Stoltenberg and Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide on Norwegian military aid, including air-defence support, and civilian assistance. On Wednesday, he joined a host of other foreign dignitaries at the funeral of Norway’s King Harald, who died on August 28, aged 89. Zelensky left Norway afterwards, headed for Canada and talks with leaders there, Store told NRK.

Guten Tag from DW's newsroom in Bonn. Things are getting increasingly tense inside Chancellor Friedrich Merz's coalition. The conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU) is piling pressure on its center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD) partners to deliver on pension and labor market reforms agreed earlier this year. And the CDU appears ready to play hardball. The gloves are also coming off at Volkswagen. Germany's IG Metall union has accused VW management of provoking a conflict "that the company cannot afford." Stay with us here for these stories and more of what Germany is talking about today. Several leading German politicians headed to central Bremen on Friday, on the eve of the anniversary of German reunification on Saturday, October 3. The public holiday's festivities are centered around the northern city of Bremen this year, because the city-state currently holds the rotating presidency of the regionalized upper house of parliament, the Bundesrat. Bremen's Mayor Andreas Bovenschulte received a delegation of some of Germany's most senior political leaders, including Chancellor Friedrich Merz , Bundestag speaker Julia Klöckner, and the state premiers of North Rhine-Westphalia, Hendrik Wüst, Baden-Würrtemberg, Cem Özdemir and Schleswig-Holstein, Daniel Günther. The group walked around the marketplace in central Bremen, with a heavy security escort in place, before posing in front of the city hall and then going inside with the mayor. On Saturday morning, a church service at Bremen's St. Peter's Cathedral at around 10 a.m. local time will get the day's schedule underway. As well as Merz, President Frank-Walter Steinmeier is expected at that service. Hundreds of people have gathered at Berlin 's central Brandenburg Gate for a demonstration and concert opposing the possibility of a return to military service, and German plans to increase defense spending . Gathered under the motto "unwzingbar," which you might translate as "incoercable" or perhaps even "unconscriptable," the crowd chanted slogans like "military service, never again," and "the rich want war, the poor want a future." Police estimated turnout early on Friday evening at about 2,000, albeit with a program that was set to continue for a few more hours, until about 9 p.m. local time. Organizers included groups like Attac, a left-leaning group primarily focused on taxation and monetary policy, the DFG-VK German Peace Association, and the IJV International Youth Association. Germany is not as yet reintroducing a period of military or civilian service , which it had for many but not all young men until as recently as 2011, but some politicians have warned it might ultimately be necessary . For now, the Bundeswehr military has started sending a questionnaire to 18-year-olds — with boys obliged to participate and girls invited to do so — seeking to gauge their theoretical interest in serving. The Bundeswehr says that this, coupled with a more general recruitment drive, has so far led to it hitting recruitment targets as it seeks to expand the ranks in the coming years. The organizers also appealed to the government to reallocate the increased spending it foresees for defense into other social areas, some of which are facing the prospect of cuts. Similar demonstrations are expected on Saturday in Berlin and Stuttgart. German investigators have seized around 33,000 CDs, records and cassettes in a major operation targeting the far-right music scene . Authorities also seized around €2 million ($2.3 million) in assets and some 130 digital devices and storage media, prosecutors and police said on Friday. Around 400 officers took part in Wednesday’s raids, which targeted four main suspects in the states of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania , Schleswig-Holstein and Bavaria . The four, aged between 43 and 55, are suspected of forming a criminal organization to produce and sell music promoting what investigators described as "National Socialist, antisemitic, racist and misanthropic ideology." More than 20,000 of the recordings were found at properties linked to the four main suspects. Properties linked to eight further suspects were searched in six other German states, while searches also took place in Estonia, Italy, Poland and the Czech Republic. Investigators said the companies searched abroad were suspected of manufacturing the recordings but were unaware of their content. No arrests were made. Authorities said the searches were aimed at gathering evidence and investigating the existing suspicions. German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier reportedly intervened in the government's recent dispute over care reform amid concerns about the survival of Chancellor Friedrich Merz's coalition. News magazine Der Spiegel reported that Steinmeier called Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil of the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD) and Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt of the conservative Christian Social Union (CSU) on Tuesday. The intervention by Germany's largely ceremonial head of state was highly unusual. Der Spiegel said Steinmeier's intervention came after he spoke with Merz on the sidelines of an event in Karlsruhe on Monday. The president reportedly returned to Berlin with the impression that the coalition could collapse and Germany could face a political crisis. The government on Friday declined to confirm the reported calls and rejected suggestions that the coalition was in crisis. Deputy government spokesperson Sebastian Hille said the government remained "capable of acting," pointing to Wednesday's cabinet agreement on care reform. He said the three governing parties were working together "well, constructively and reliably," and accused the media of placing disagreements at the top of a "conflict escalation scale." German department store chain Galeria has filed for insolvency for the fourth time in six years, putting the future of some 12,000 employees in doubt. A spokesperson for the Düsseldorf district court said the application was filed on Friday morning. Galeria said its 83 stores would remain open for the time being. The Verdi trade union blamed "outrageous management mistakes" for the latest crisis and demanded rapid answers about what would happen to employees. "Employees need a plan for the future now, not smoke and mirrors," Verdi retail chief Silke Zimmer said. Galeria previously filed for insolvency in 2020, 2022 and 2024. Its most recent difficulties followed the collapse of Austrian investor Rene Benko's Signa empire , its former parent company. A consortium comprising US investment firm NRDC Equity Partners and entrepreneur Bernd Beetz's BB Kapital SA took over Galeria in 2024. Benko, who once controlled Galeria as well as Berlin's KaDeWe luxury department store, is currently serving a prison sentence for fraud . Germany's emerging economic recovery remains fragile despite an improving outlook, the country's foreign trade association BGA has warned. A BGA survey found companies reporting improved business conditions after diversifying supply and distribution routes and adapting to recent crises. However, many firms said red tape was hampering their operations. "Companies can see light at the end of the tunnel again, but they are still driving with the handbrake on," BGA President Dirk Jandura said. Leading German economic institutes have raised their growth forecast for this year to 1.3%, up from 0.6% in their spring forecast. The government is also expected to raise its forecast next week. Debt-financed government spending on infrastructure and defense is a major driver of the expected growth. Jandura said bureaucracy remained a significant drag, with 82% of companies surveyed naming it as one of the biggest obstacles to competitiveness and 78% saying they had yet to notice any reduction in red tape. The improvement has also yet to reach the labor market, according to BGA, with more companies in the sector planning to cut jobs than create them. Germany's IG Metall union has sharply criticized Volkswagen over its latest cost-cutting drive, accusing management of provoking a conflict "that the company cannot afford." Thorsten Gröger, IG Metall's regional head for Lower Saxony and Saxony-Anhalt, told public broadcaster Deutschlandfunk that VW's approach was "disrespectful toward its own employees" and "irresponsible toward the company itself." Gröger said worker representatives had listened to a 50-minute presentation from management without hearing "a single word" about plans to terminate key collective bargaining agreements, while the media had already been informed. He described the move as "unprecedented in the history of Volkswagen" and said employee representatives were prepared for the dispute. VW says employment conditions need to be revised because of mounting cost pressures. The carmaker plans to cut 50,000 jobs worldwide in the coming years, on top of previously announced reductions. Around half of the additional cuts could come in Germany. The longer-term future of entire VW plants in Emden, Hannover and Zwickau, as well as Audi's Neckarsulm site, also remains uncertain. Germany's conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU) is stepping up pressure on its center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD) coalition partners ahead of talks next week on a series of contested economic and social reforms. CDU General Secretary Franziska Hoppermann said Labor Minister Bärbel Bas, who is also an SPD co-leader, needed to produce legislation on pension reform "so that we can finally negotiate concretely." Her comments to the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung (FAZ) newspaper come as Chancellor Friedrich Merz prepares to bring labor market reforms before the coalition committee next week. Merz said this week that Germany had "some catching up to do" when it came to making the labor market more flexible. The Handelsblatt newspaper reported that CDU parliamentary leaders were considering withholding support for Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil's income tax reform until Bas submits legislation on pensions and the labor market. One government official described the increasingly fraught atmosphere as "real traffic-light vibes," according to the Handelsblatt , a reference to the bitter disputes that preceded the collapse of former Chancellor Olaf Scholz's three-party "traffic light coalition." The CDU argues that reforms agreed by the coalition in July were a package and that the SPD cannot expect its preferred measures to go ahead while delaying concessions it made on pensions and the labor market. Among the most contentious plans is the proposed abolition of penalty-free early retirement after 45 years of contributions. The measure faces opposition within the SPD as well as from several CDU state premiers. Photograph: Courtesy of NYPD A man was shot and killed in a New York City subway station Saturday afternoon, and the New York police department is searching for the suspect. The suspect fatally shot a man in his 30s on the E train platform of the 53rd Street-7th Avenue subway station, according to a statement from the NYPD . “On Saturday, October 17, 2026, at approximately 12:21 PM, on the northbound E train platform of the 53rd Street–7th Avenue subway station in Manhattan, this individual shot and killed a man in his 30s,” the NYPD’s statement said. According to the NYPD, the suspect displayed a firearm and discharged it, striking the victim once in the chest. EMS responded and transported the victim to NYC health + hospitals/Bellevue, where he was pronounced deceased. The identity of the victim is not known at this time. The suspect is wanted for homicide within the confines of the Midtown North Precinct/Transit District 1. The NYPD released surveillance photos of the suspect, who fled on foot and headed northbound on 7th Avenue. The images show the suspect dressed in a red tracksuit, a black vest and a black face mask and carrying a backpack. Authorities are urging individuals with information regarding the incident to reach out to its tip line at 1-800-577-TIPS (8477), or submit tips online at the Crime Stoppers website or via X @NYPDTips. The investigation remains ongoing. https://hvg.hu/eurologus/20261110_orosz-.text: Az ukrajnai háború lezárásáról és az esetleges békemegállapodás biztonsági feltételeiről egyeztettek kedden Abu-Dzabiban az európai partnerek, Ukrajna és az Egyesült Államok képviselői. A találkozó közös nyilatkozata szerint a résztvevők olyan biztonsági keretrendszer kialakítására törekednek, amely hosszú távon garantálhatja Ukrajna biztonságát, és megteremtheti a tárgyalásos rendezés feltételeit. Egyértelművé tették azt is, hogy bármilyen megállapodásnak tiszteletben kell tartania Ukrajna szuverenitását, területi integritását és önálló döntéshozatalát. A nyilatkozat hangsúlyozza, hogy a háború lezárása után az európai biztonsági rendszer megerősítésére is szükség lesz. A résztvevők a meglévő európai biztonsági intézményekre és megállapodásokra építenének, miközben olyan mechanizmusokat alakítanának ki, amelyek csökkentik egy újabb konfliktus és a veszélyes eszkaláció kockázatát. A NATO továbbra is az euroatlanti kollektív védelem központi pillére maradna. A közlemény végén a felek azt is rögzítették, hogy a tárgyalási folyamat során szoros együttműködésben maradnak, és szélesebb körű, az európai partnereket is bevonó többoldalú egyeztetések felé kívánnak elmozdulni. Hogy ez pontosan mikor és milyen formában történhet meg, arról egyelőre nincs döntés. Paola Pinho, az Európai Bizottság szóvivője a testület keddi sajtótájékoztatóján elmondta, hogy Abu-Dzabiban két külön egyeztetésre került sor. Az elsőn az Európai Unió, a Franciaországból, Németországból és az Egyesült Királyságból álló E3-csoport, Olaszország és a NATO képviselői találkoztak az ukrán delegációval. Ezt követte az a megbeszélés, amelyen már az Egyesült Államok képviselői is részt vettek, és amelyről a közös nyilatkozat készült. A szóvivő szerint az európaiak részvétele természetes, hiszen „Ukrajna biztonsága nyilvánvalóan Európa biztonsága is”. Arra a kérdésre azonban, hogy a nyilatkozatban említett szélesebb körű tárgyalások azt jelentik-e, hogy az európaiak nem vesznek részt közvetlenül az oroszokkal folytatott abu-dzabi egyeztetéseken, nem adott egyértelmű választ. Mint mondta, a kétnapos találkozósorozat különböző összetételű megbeszélésekből áll, a többoldalú tárgyalások időpontja pedig „még nem látható”. A közvetlen európai–orosz tárgyalások lehetőségét tehát nem zárta ki. Pinho megerősítette azt is, hogy az EU nem változtatott Ukrajna területi integritásával kapcsolatos álláspontján. Donald Trump amerikai elnöknek arra a kijelentésére reagálva, hogy Ukrajna a rendezés után „egy kicsit más formájú” lehet, a szóvivő a közös nyilatkozatra hivatkozott. Ez az az álláspont, amelyet az EU eddig is képviselt, és amelyet ezeken a találkozókon is képvisel – mondta. Arra viszont, hogy Brüsszel elfogadna-e egy olyan megállapodást, amelynek nyomán egyes ukrán területek orosz irányítás alatt maradnának, nem adott közvetlen választ. Úgy fogalmazott, hogy ebben a kérdésben Ukrajna álláspontja a döntő. A sajtótájékoztatón az is kiderült, hogy az Abu-Dzabiban egyeztető európai csoport a korábbi francia–német–brit hármashoz képest Olaszországgal bővült. Arra a kérdésre, hogy ki kezdeményezte Róma bevonását, illetve csatlakozhatnak-e további országok, például Lengyelország, Pinho az olasz kormányhoz irányította az újságírókat. A 27 uniós tagállam vezetői a hét későbbi részében, az informális Európai Tanács ülésén is megvitatják az ukrajnai békefolyamatot.
